race.name: Khomas100
race.tagline: Windhoek to Gross Barmen on 143 kilometers of fast, rugged Namibian gravel.

adventure.explanation: A point-to-point crossing from Windhoek to Gross Barmen through Namibia's open Khomas landscape is the rare qualifier with the character of a destination expedition.

altitude.explanation: Windhoek sits high enough for thinner air to be noticeable to sea-level visitors, although this is not an extreme-altitude race.

climate.explanation: Dry air, sun exposure, dust, wind, and long gaps across open Namibian terrain make environmental management part of the race rather than background scenery.

community.explanation: The event has a meaningful Namibian identity and continental-championship role, but its broader gravel culture remains small compared with established global festivals.

elevation.explanation: The organizer lists approximately 2,300 meters, or 7,546 feet, of climbing on the 143-kilometer full route.

expenses.explanation: The entry itself is affordable, but flights to Namibia and point-to-point travel logistics make the total trip expensive for most international riders.

experience.explanation: The remote landscape, point-to-point format, and finish at Gross Barmen give the race a strong sense of place beyond its championship labels.

field_depth.explanation: UCI qualification and African Continental Championship titles attract serious racers, though the international field is not yet proven at top global depth.

length.explanation: The full championship route is 143 kilometers, or 88.9 miles.

logistics.explanation: This is a point-to-point race from Tony Rust Race Track to Gross Barmen Resort, with mandatory GPS navigation and remote-course planning layered onto international travel.

prestige.explanation: The combination of UCI Gravel World Series status and the CAC African Continental Gravel Championship gives real significance without an iconic multi-decade legacy.

race_quality.explanation: Published routes, six water points, category-specific starts, cutoffs, prize money, age-group podiums, and championship sanction indicate a professionally structured event.

technicality.explanation: The route is mostly unsurfaced and requires 40-50 mm tires plus mandatory GPS, but the organizer frames it as fast gravel and rolling terrain rather than extreme trail riding.

value.explanation: A full-distance entry of N$1,200 before the late period is strong local value for both UCI and continental-championship racing.

cultural_impact.explanation: Serving as an African Continental Gravel Championship gives the race regional importance beyond its participant count.

course_description.character: A point-to-point route that leaves Windhoek on pavement before committing to long, exposed stretches of mostly unsurfaced road toward Gross Barmen.

suffering_zones.label: Windhoek opener
suffering_zones.description: The full-distance field starts at Tony Rust Race Track and must avoid over-racing the early paved and climbing-heavy section.

suffering_zones.label: Khomas gravel
suffering_zones.description: Long unsurfaced sectors, dust, wind, and mandatory GPS navigation make attention and self-management as important as raw fitness.

suffering_zones.label: Water Point 5 cutoff
suffering_zones.description: Riders must reach the fifth water point by 15:00 and maintain at least a 16 km/h average to remain on course.

course_description.signature_challenge: Carry speed across exposed Namibian gravel without losing hydration, navigation, or pacing control before the Gross Barmen finish.

logistics.overview: The full route starts at 07:00 from Tony Rust Race Track in Windhoek and finishes at NWR Gross Barmen Resort near Okahandja.
logistics.accommodation: The point-to-point finish at Gross Barmen Resort makes lodging and return transport part of the race plan.
logistics.getting_there: International riders fly into Windhoek and must coordinate start access plus post-finish transport from Gross Barmen.
logistics.parking: Start and finish are in different locations; confirm vehicle and shuttle arrangements in the rider guide.
logistics.spectator_info: Prize ceremonies at Gross Barmen are scheduled separately for elite and age-group fields.

climate.overview: The exposed Namibian course demands a conservative hydration and sun-management plan even during the dry-season race window.
climate.wind_conditions: Open plains offer little shelter from crosswinds or headwinds.
climate.altitude_effects: Windhoek's elevation can be noticeable to sea-level riders, especially before the course begins trending toward the finish.

terrain.terrain_overview: Mostly unsurfaced Namibian roads connect rolling hills, faster plains, sustained climbs, and exposed descents.
terrain.key_features: 143 kilometers, approximately 2,300 meters of climbing, mandatory GPS, six water points, and a point-to-point finish.

history.overview: Khomas100 is a Namibian gravel fixture that adds both UCI Gravel World Series and CAC African Continental Gravel Championship status in 2026.
history.notable_editions: 2026 combines the Khomas100 title, African Continental Championship, and UCI World Series qualification in one race.
history.growth_trajectory: A national endurance event is developing into one of Africa's internationally sanctioned gravel races.

editions.note: First year as a UCI Gravel World Series race and CAC African Continental Gravel Championship.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast-looking course whose remoteness, climbing, and Namibian exposure make it anything but easy.
final_verdict.best_for: Self-sufficient riders who want championship stakes and an uncommon gravel destination.
final_verdict.not_ideal_for: Anyone uncomfortable with remote navigation, point-to-point logistics, dust, or sustained sun exposure.
final_verdict.pro_tip: Treat the mandatory GPS and six-water-point plan as race equipment, not administrative details, and organize finish transport before arrival.
